notes: ChatGPT's A15 answer (DEPTH2 package, clock-and-tax/local-income-tax-routing.json) established Ohio Revised Code 718.04 municipal income-tax authority and Philadelphia's Wage and Earnings Tax as one tax. The game's policy catalog now lists income tax as decided by states and municipalities. Whether a particular city may levy one is answered by the fiscal-authority corpus (src/fiscal-authority/query.ts), which today holds only Alaska records, so no city or county anywhere may levy an income tax in play.

This container could not reach codes.ohio.gov (the proxy refused the connection), so the Ohio statute could not be acquired into data/source/state-local-fiscal-authority. A first-party copy of each authorizing statute, as retrievable page text or PDF with its URL and retrieval date, is what the corpus needs.
question: In which of the 52 jurisdictions (the 50 states, D.C. and Puerto Rico) may a municipality, a county, or a school district levy a tax on individual income or wages, and under what authority? For each jurisdiction and each of those three levels: authorized, authorized with voter approval, authorized for named places only, or not authorized; the statute or constitutional section and its official URL; the effective date of the authority; any statewide rate cap; and whether residents get a credit for income tax paid to another local government.
requestedBy: Issue voting and city taxes thread

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Ohio municipal authority and Philadelphia's single tax only. States explicitly that it is not a national survey and does not establish county authority.
The schema already has INDIVIDUAL_INCOME_TAX and LOCAL_INCOME_TAX_TYPE fields but no production record fills them for any state.

title: Where cities and counties may levy an income tax
usableAnswer: A 52-row by three-level table: authorization status, citation with official URL, effective date, rate cap, voter-approval requirement and resident credit rule, one row per jurisdiction and level, with 'not authorized' stated explicitly rather than left blank. Named-place authority (such as a single city) listed by place.
whyItMatters: A city income tax should exist only where the city really has the power. Today none exists anywhere, which is wrong for Ohio, Pennsylvania, Michigan and others; granting it everywhere would be wrong for most states.
